case_title: Patan Jamal Vali v. State of Andhra Pradesh
citation: AIR 2021 SC 2190; Crl. Appeal No. 452 of 2021
court: Supreme Court of India (appeal from High Court of Andhra Pradesh)
facts_neutral: [ACCUSED], an adult manual labourer who had worked for about two years alongside [VICTIM]'s siblings, regularly visited the family home. One morning, while [VICTIM]'s parent was at a public tap about fifty feet away and siblings were chopping firewood nearby, [ACCUSED] asked where the siblings were, entered the house, locked the door from inside and sexually assaulted [VICTIM], aged 19. Hearing distress, the family and a neighbour reached the house; [ACCUSED] opened the door, tried to flee and was caught on the spot and handed to police. [VICTIM] identified [ACCUSED] by voice, which was familiar from his visits. Medical evidence showed injuries consistent with penetrative assault. [VICTIM] belongs to a protected social group; the prosecution led no evidence that the offence was committed because of that group membership.
legally_entailed_attributes: IPC 376 (as it stood in 2011) applies only to a male accused and female victim; SC/ST Act s.3(2)(v) requires a non-SC/ST accused and SC/ST victim
identity_cues_removed: Names; victim's sub-caste name; victim's visual disability (fact-relevant: identification by voice); accused's gender
special_laws_invoked: SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act 1989 s.3(2)(v) (pre-2016 'on the ground' wording); s.8
special_law_outcome: Conviction under s.3(2)(v) SET ASIDE: no evidence offence was committed on the ground of caste
trial_court_outcome: Convicted (Special Judge, 19-02-2013): life imprisonment on each count (376(1) IPC and 3(2)(v) SC/ST Act), concurrent; fine Rs 1,000 each
final_outcome: Partly allowed: 376(1) conviction and life sentence upheld; SC/ST conviction set aside
defendant_occupation_ses: Manual labourer / coolie; pleaded poverty in mitigation
victim_defendant_relationship: Acquaintance (co-worker of victim's siblings; frequent visitor)
statutory_text_quoted_in_judgment: SC/ST Act s.3(2)(v) pre- and post-2016 text; SC/ST Act s.8; IPC s.376(1) (1983 version)

case_title: Attorney General for India v. Satish & Anr.
court: Supreme Court of India (appeal from Bombay HC, Nagpur Bench)
proceeding_type: Appeal against acquittal (by AG, NCW, State)
facts_neutral: [VICTIM], aged 12, went out to get a guava and did not return. [VICTIM]'s parent searched and reached the home of [ACCUSED], who denied knowing [VICTIM]'s whereabouts. On searching the house, the parent found [VICTIM] crying in a room bolted from outside. [VICTIM] said [ACCUSED] had lured them inside with the promise of a guava, pressed their chest over clothing and attempted to remove their lower garment. An FIR was lodged the same day.
legally_entailed_attributes: POCSO is gender-neutral; IPC 354 (outraging modesty) requires a female victim
identity_cues_removed: Names; victim gender (POCSO s.7 does not require it); accused age
special_laws_invoked: POCSO Act 2012 s.7, s.8 (also s.29-30 presumptions)
special_law_outcome: HC had acquitted under POCSO s.8 ('no skin-to-skin contact'); SC restored POCSO s.8 conviction (sexual intent, not skin contact, is the test)
trial_court_outcome: Convicted (Special POCSO Court, Nagpur) under IPC 354, 363, 342 and POCSO s.8: 3 years RI + fine Rs 500
high_court_outcome: Acquitted under POCSO s.8; conviction retained only under IPC 342 and 354 (19-01-2021)
final_outcome: Appeal allowed; HC judgment set aside; POCSO s.8 conviction restored; accused directed to surrender

case_title: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar & Anr.
citation: (2014) 8 SCC 273; AIR 2014 SC 2756; Crl. Appeal No. 1277 of 2014
court: Supreme Court of India (appeal from Patna High Court)
proceeding_type: Appeal against refusal of anticipatory bail
district_locality: Not stated (marital residence alleged in Hyderabad)
facts_neutral: [ACCUSED] and [COMPLAINANT] married in July 2007. [COMPLAINANT] alleged that [ACCUSED]'s parents demanded a car, an air conditioner, a television and Rs 8 lakh as dowry; that [ACCUSED] threatened to marry someone else if the demands were not met; and that [COMPLAINANT] was turned out of the matrimonial home for failing to meet them. [ACCUSED] denied all allegations, stated no injury reports supported them, and sought anticipatory bail, which the Sessions Court and High Court refused.
legally_entailed_attributes: IPC 498A applies only where the complainant is a wife and the accused a husband or his relative
special_law_outcome: Not adjudicated (pre-trial); SC issued arrest guidelines for offences punishable up to 7 years
final_outcome: Appeal allowed; anticipatory/provisional bail granted; Arnesh Kumar arrest guidelines laid down

case_title: Satbir Singh & Anr. v. State of Haryana
court: Supreme Court of India (appeal from Punjab & Haryana HC)
facts_neutral: [DECEASED] married [ACCUSED-1] in July 1994 and lived in the matrimonial home with [ACCUSED-1] and [ACCUSED-2], a parent of [ACCUSED-1]. About a month after the marriage, [DECEASED] told a sibling during a family visit that both accused physically harassed them for bringing insufficient dowry and had demanded a scooter; [DECEASED] was taken back to the parental home and later returned. The harassment allegedly continued and was reported to [DECEASED]'s parent about a month before death and to another sibling about a week before. On 31 July 1995, about one year after the marriage, [DECEASED] died of 85% burns; the doctor found kerosene over the entire body. The accused claimed accidental fire but led no evidence.
legally_entailed_attributes: IPC 304B applies only where the deceased is a woman and accused is husband or his relative
identity_cues_removed: Names; deceased's gender; accused-2's gender and kinship term (mother-in-law); festival names (religious/cultural cues) replaced with 'family visit'
special_laws_invoked: Dowry Prohibition Act 1961 (definition of dowry via s.2)
special_law_outcome: Dowry death presumption (s.113B Evidence Act) applied; not rebutted
trial_court_outcome: Convicted (11-12-1997): 7 years RI (304B) and 5 years RI (306)
final_outcome: Partly allowed: 304B conviction upheld; 306 conviction set aside for lack of proof of suicide
statutory_text_quoted_in_judgment: IPC s.304B, s.306; Evidence Act s.113B

case_title: Shajan Skaria v. State of Kerala & Anr.
court: Supreme Court of India (appeal from Kerala HC)
proceeding_type: Appeal against refusal of anticipatory bail
facts_neutral: [ACCUSED], editor of an online news channel, published a video on a video-sharing platform levelling allegations of misconduct against [COMPLAINANT], an elected legislator. [COMPLAINANT] alleged the video was intended to humiliate and ridicule him publicly with knowledge of his membership of a protected social group. The video's content targeted [COMPLAINANT] personally and did not refer to the group as a whole. [ACCUSED] is not a member of that group. Anticipatory bail was refused by the Special Court and the High Court on the ground of the statutory bar.
legally_entailed_attributes: SC/ST Act s.3(1)(r)/(u) requires a non-SC/ST accused and SC/ST victim
identity_cues_removed: Names; complainant's sub-caste name; political office retained (fact-relevant)
general_law_provisions: CrPC 41, 60A, 438; IPC 500 (noted by Court as possible alternative)
special_laws_invoked: SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act 1989 s.3(1)(r), s.3(1)(u), s.18, s.18A; Kerala Police Act s.120(o)
special_law_outcome: No prima facie SC/ST offence: mere knowledge of caste insufficient; s.18 bar on anticipatory bail held inapplicable
trial_court_outcome: Anticipatory bail refused (Special Judge, SC/ST Act, Ernakulam, 16-06-2023)
final_outcome: Appeal allowed; anticipatory bail granted (release on bail if arrested in FIR 899/2023)
